target.title: fix(auto-reply): support custom silent tokens with digits and punctuation in prefix matcher
target.body:
Fixes #99982

## What Problem This Solves

`isSilentReplyPrefixText` never matches custom silent tokens containing digits or punctuation (e.g., `NOREPLY2`, `NO-ANSWER`). The character guard `/[^A-Z_]/.test(normalized)` at L304 of `src/auto-reply/tokens.ts` rejects any input containing non-letter characters, causing streamed prefix detection to fail for custom tokens with digits/hyphens.

This means the streaming suppression path effectively ignores custom silent tokens that include numbers or special characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The character guard was too broad — it checked the **input fragment** (the streamed prefix) instead of the **token definition**. An input fragment is inherently transient and partial; the only meaningful question is whether the token itself is safe for prefix matching.

- Custom tokens containing non-letter characters (digits, hyphens) cannot be mistaken for natural language words, so their partial prefixes are safe.
- The underscore guard (`normalized.includes("_")`) is preserved for standard `A-Z_` tokens like `HEARTBEAT_OK`.
- The `/[^A-Z_]/.test(tokenUpper)` check now tests the **token**, not the fragment.

## User Impact

Before: custom silent tokens like `"NOREPLY2"` or `"NO-ANSWER"` never match in the streaming prefix matcher, delaying silent-reply classification until the full token is received.

After: prefix fragments of custom tokens (e.g., `"NORE"` for `"NOREPLY2"`, `"NO-AN"` for `"NO-ANSWER"`) are correctly recognized during streaming.

All 42 tests pass (original 39 + 3 new).

## Evidence

- Implementation: `src/auto-reply/tokens.ts`
- Tests: `src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts`
- Test suite: `pnpm test src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts` — 42 passed
- `git diff --numstat`: 2 files changed, 44 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

## AI Assistance

This commit was co-authored with AI. The AI implemented the fix, tests, and PR description under human supervision. See `https://docs.openclaw.ai/contributing/ai` for AI contribution policy.
